title: A value or the reason why not
description:
`std::optional` says a result is missing but not **why**. `std::expected<T, E>` (C++23, in `<expected>`) holds either a value or an error.

Using the `AgeError` enum provided, write:

- `std::expected<int, AgeError> parseAge(std::string_view text)`
  - empty text: `AgeError::empty`
  - not entirely a whole number: `AgeError::notANumber`
  - below 0 or above 150: `AgeError::outOfRange`
  - otherwise the age
- `std::string report(const std::expected<int, AgeError>& result)`: `"age 42"`, or `"error: empty"`, `"error: not a number"`, `"error: out of range"`.

Return an error with `return std::unexpected{ AgeError::empty };`
